speakers.title: Senior Vice President of Investor Relations

speakers.name: Ilya Yuffa
speakers.title: President of Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities

exchanges.question: At a high level, what do Lilly's margins look like across a wide range of incretin price scenarios, and how do manufacturing investments add to the competitive moat?
exchanges.answer: Five or six quarters into the post-shortage world, obesity behaves differently from other pharma: with 75% of ex-U.S. Mounjaro business out of pocket and a meaningful U.S. portion, volume expands, perhaps non-linearly, with price cuts, subject to a floor. Q1 price effects were mainly negotiated government outcomes (MFN package with the Trump administration; China diabetes access at a meaningful price cut) where volume far outstripped the concession. Unit economics are driven by fixed sunk or unmovable costs, giving latitude at the margin; R&D investment is the 'X factor' for long-term operating margin.

exchanges.question: What are the learnings from the better-than-expected international Mounjaro launch and longer-term ramp, and will generic semaglutide entry in select markets affect it?
exchanges.answer: Mounjaro is fully launched in more than 55 countries with rapid share gains; Brazil and Korea (launched H2 2025) are at an estimated 60% share, plus China type 2 NRDL reimbursement. In India, with a few weeks of data, generics are stimulating overall obesity market growth and Mounjaro prescriptions are about 10% higher than before generic entry. International share averages above 53%, so further share gains get harder; expect strong year-on-year and some sequential growth driven by patient activation, with H2 European holiday seasonality.

exchanges.question: How will the obesity market segment as retatrutide, Foundayo and eloralintide arrive, and where does each open up the market?
exchanges.answer: With patients possibly numbering in the billions, the market is in early innings of tailoring: single agonists, dual agonists and now orals as a third segment. Retatrutide suits those seeking greater weight loss but has opportunities across the spectrum; eloralintide could serve patients wanting a non-GLP-1 mechanism for tolerability, or as an add-on to incretins; Lilly is also investing in less-frequent dosing, added metabolic benefits and ultra-long-acting genetic approaches. Ultimate mix is hard to predict; many share common manufacturing platforms Lilly is investing in.

exchanges.question: What is the strategy and timing (Q4 versus 2027) to activate Medicare patients, and how will the price point affect persistence?
exchanges.responderTitle: President of Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities
exchanges.answer: Part D access for obesity starts in July, with millions of obese Part D beneficiaries and Bridge running through 2027; uptake will be a gradual path in 2026 with continued growth in 2027 as physicians, pharmacies and consumers are educated. Zepbound and Mounjaro already have great persistency relative to other chronic conditions, and the $50 a month copay should add to that.

exchanges.question: What must I&I, neuroscience or oncology achieve to match the scale of the obesity/metabolic business, and is it BD or something else?
exchanges.answer: Those businesses are growing extremely fast; even without obesity and metabolic, Lilly would be the fastest or one of the fastest-growing pharma companies. Each area has significant unmet need to scale into, and BD will also contribute, e.g. Centessa for sleep-wake and Orna for immune reset.

exchanges.question: How confident is Lilly in the Foundayo launch-curve framing (starting below oral Wegovy, accelerating in H2) given about 15,000 patients started so far; and what Foundayo contribution is in the raised guide?
exchanges.responderTitle: President of Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities
exchanges.answer: Early days: active salesforce promotion began just over a week ago and broad channel availability two weeks ago; over 8,000 prescribers, a third of whom had not written an oral GLP-1; commercial access at two large PBMs by middle of May, Medicare from beginning of July; just over 20,000 patients treated, 80% new to class; full-scale DTC and TV in Q3. Montarce: the guide raise reflects the whole portfolio; with three weeks of data Foundayo is tracking to the plan set at the start of the year; no specific Foundayo contribution given.

exchanges.question: With Bridge extended into 2027, what is next for Balance, and is Lilly working to secure longer-term Medicare access?
exchanges.answer: The 2027 extension was a contingency if Part D plans did not opt in at a certain rate, which they did not, given their margins and other Part D disruptions. $50 a month access over an 18-month window should drive persistency and could show population-level health improvements, setting up the 2028 discussion where Ricks expects the government to push hard for Part D plan participation and normalizing obesity care. More news probably as 2026 exits on actual 2028 plans.

exchanges.question: What are the mechanics of the Employer Connect program and the steps to convince employers to opt in?
exchanges.responderTitle: President of Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities
exchanges.answer: Commercial access has been steady around 50%; Employer Connect works with third parties to approach employers, offering a transparent price and flexible employer-employee contribution design. The 2026 selling cycle has passed, so impact will most likely be gradual in the back half of 2026 with incremental opt-ins for 2027; real-world evidence on health and productivity should reinforce coverage decisions.

exchanges.question: How will Lilly leverage its scale across the incretin portfolio in the DTC channel, and can portfolio scale help drive commercial coverage?
exchanges.answer: Consumer-driven digital health is here to stay and a big part of the business; expect continuous improvement and expansion, potentially as a platform for future preventative medicines, within regulations. Yuffa: around 55% of Zepbound new patient starts are self-pay, mostly via LillyDirect or telehealth, and about 45% of early Foundayo volume comes through LillyDirect. Jonsson: OUS share is already very high, so patient activation drives growth, though with a slower ramp; the commercial coverage part was not directly addressed.

exchanges.question: Q1 U.S. Zepbound of 7 million TRx and $4.1 billion implies about $580 per prescription (about $550 adjusted) versus roughly $450 cash price; what explains the delta, or is IMS missing online channels?
exchanges.answer: The math is 'pretty spot on'; excluding the November MFN agreement and NRDL access prices, pricing has been relatively stable quarter-on-quarter, and LillyDirect prices, cut starting in December, have been stable; the remainder by difference is the commercial business that gets to the net $550. Ricks added that a reasonable amount of medical exception and OSA usage moves across channels at close to an undiscounted price.

exchanges.question: How does the Foundayo launch compare with a traditional primary care launch, what is being accelerated or held back and why, given large pre-built inventory?
exchanges.responderTitle: President of Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities
exchanges.answer: Same three elements as other primary care launches, but access is faster (two of three PBMs in coming weeks, Part D in July); digital, social and out-of-home DTC began in week one, while full DTC is held until physicians understand the profile, though still earlier than normal. Ricks: the three major U.S. obesity products are line extensions, so Foundayo starts from a much lower awareness baseline; inventory supports international rollouts with 40 countries under review and launches expected as Lilly exits this year into next year in scaled markets.

exchanges.question: What is the vision for regular U.S. employer insurance coverage of obesity drugs versus models with greater out-of-pocket cost-sharing via LillyDirect?
exchanges.answer: Lilly believes obesity medicines should be broadly covered; July 1 Medicare may spill over into commercial, and the category should eventually resemble diabetes and hypertension markets, but not in a straight line. With 70% of adults overweight or obese, it is easier for payers to say no; Employer Connect creates alternate pathways, data will show cost-effectiveness as prices trend down, and new indications in comorbid populations are an unlock; expect incremental quarter-on-quarter progress.
